text:
sarah: Quick one — SOC auditor called out missing operator-level evidence for BYOK HSM imports (window 2026-03-10 -> 2026-03-15). They want chain-of-custody: operator identity, signed import receipts, and audit trail. Who has the canonical records?
kevin: I think importer writes to s3://redwood-hsm-audit and streams to kinesis. But we redacted some operator fields for ephemeral sessions. :grimacing:
emma: Correct — importer service emits two places: /var/log/hsm-importer (node) and the audit topic. The node logs include operator uid only when JIT flag is set. We defaulted JIT off for a while.
josh: We do keep HSM attestation blobs (CBOR) in the import job output. Example: ```{attestation: "MEYCIQ...", key_fp: "ab:cd:ef:01"}``` Those are signed by HSM but not always tied to a named operator if operator session was ephemeral.
sarah: Auditor specifically wants operator UID + proof that an operator approved the import (signed OTP or dual-operator sign-off).
emma: We have dual-operator flow in the design doc but it wasn't enforced for some tenants until last month. I can check feature flag history.
sec-bot: Alert: 2026-03-12 03:14Z — import-job-789 failed authz check (operator: <redacted>) — metadata written to redwood-hsm-audit/2026/03/12/import-job-789.json
kevin: If we can pull the raw JSON for that range we might correlate session IDs to SSO logs (OKTA). Command: `aws s3api get-object --bucket redwood-hsm-audit --key 2026/03/12/import-job-789.json out.json`
josh: I'll grep for session IDs and cross-ref with okta: `jq -r .session_id out.json | xargs -I{} aws logs filter-log-events --log-group /okta/events --filter-pattern '{}'`
legal: Quick note — if operator UIDs map to personal data in certain jurisdictions, retention/transfer requires justification. Auditors will accept pseudonymous IDs if we can prove mapping exists and controls on re-identification.
sarah: Good call. For the auditor I think we need: (1) raw import job JSONs, (2) HSM attestation blobs, (3) okta session records mapping session_id -> user, (4) change history for the RBAC/JIT flag.
emma: I'll pull feature-flag toggles and the importer's deploy history. There might be a period where JIT was off due to a rollback (around 2026-03-11).
kevin: RBAC change req: propose a new role `hsm_import_operator` + `hsm_import_witness`. Both require MFA and session recording. We should log: operator_uid, session_id, action=import, key_fingerprint, attestation_blob_ref, trust_anchor_sig, and request_id.
josh: Also add a non-repudiation field: we can persist the HSM signature and a signed-statement by the operator (signed with platform key) to bind them. Implementation: operator signs the import request with their platform SSH key; we store that signed request in S3 alongside attestation.
legal: That approach sounds reasonable from a compliance POV but confirm encryption-at-rest for these artifacts and access controls for re-identification. Also export controls if keys cross borders.
emma: Implementation note — collecting operator signatures means we need a short-lived signing key provisioner. That ties into KMS integration: Do we store platform signing keys in customer KMS or our HSM? For BYOK customers we cannot escrow their key. We can use tenant-scoped ephemeral signing keys minted by our KMS-proxy and logged.
kevin: For BYOK, never escrow customer keys. Use our ephemeral signing keys (not key material for customer keys) to sign operator approval statements. Store mapping in audit index so only authorized roles (sec, legal, cust-support with court order) can request mapping.
sarah: Action items: Emma = export import-job JSONs + deploy history (due EOD). Josh = correlate session_ids to okta logs and produce mapping (store securely). Kevin = draft RBAC role change PR and audit-schema changes. Legal = confirm retention window and redaction requirements.
josh: I'll put the correlation script in a gist and mark it internal. Quick snippet: ```session_ids=( $(jq -r '.session_id' *.json) ); for s in "${session_ids[@]}"; do aws logs filter-log-events --log-group /okta/events --filter-pattern "$s" --start-time 1700000000000; done```
sec-bot: Note: please tag findings with #audit-evidence and upload to secure bucket with kms:key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/xxxx for encrypted-at-rest storage.
sarah: Thanks — please report back here when each item is uploaded. Auditor is expecting a bundle by next Wednesday. :eyes:
